atoms.label: contradicted
atoms.rationale: D1 explicitly identifies separate API-server and engine-core processes within the V1 architecture. D2 independently states that API scale-out can run four API processes and one or two engine-core processes, providing an available configuration inconsistent with always sharing one process.
atoms.ambiguity_note: D3 describes caching conditional on a one-to-one correspondence between API P0 and engine-core P1 processes. Under a strict entailment reading, it does not independently assert that the antecedent is realized or realizable, so D3 is excluded as a minimal contradiction proofset. A pragmatic reading of documented IPC behavior as an available distinct-process configuration could instead admit [D3]. The full-evidence contradicted label is unambiguous.

atoms.label: insufficient
atoms.rationale: The passages describe file size, storage layout, view relationships, and alignment. They state neither a universal CPU serialization-time benefit from cloning nor a counterexample to that timing claim. Smaller storage does not by itself establish CPU-time behavior.

atoms.label: contradicted
atoms.rationale: D1 explicitly requires every array task to complete successfully. D3 independently describes afterok on the array ID as waiting for the entire array to complete successfully, contradicting satisfaction merely from one successful task.
